narrative: The original PR removed the './terminal' export but updated only CLAUDE.md. The F1 sweep fix (232fd6f) caused almost every later finding: a missing JSONC comma, invented wildcard subpath notation pasted into three docs, a carried-over '404' claim, and a missed src/terminal tree in IMPL.md. The agent's doc fixes asserted new facts (wildcard exports, 404) without checking package.json; a fix that adds prose needs the same source check as the original change.
The agent ran the pushback check correctly on F5 by citing the commit that added the comma.

narrative: This PR is an audit report that contained factual errors itself: a wrong count, a fabricated 'methods do not exist' finding backed by a grep that was quoted but never run, an inconsistent test breakdown, and wrong file claims. Only F7 came from a fix (the '(#)' link added for F2). F8-F10 were pre-existing errors the reviewer surfaced across later rounds, and F1 was a reviewer hallucination the agent correctly rejected.
guidance_observations: An audit report's own claims need the same mechanical verification it demands of the docs; every 'X does not exist' and every count should be backed by a command actually run.
The reviewer drip-fed pre-existing errors across rounds 2 and 3, so in a fact-heavy report the author's own full re-verification pass before the first push is the only way to avoid those rounds.

narrative: This PR added a canonical tmux-compat module and docs. Round 0 flagged a relative link and missing unit tests, and both were accepted. Round 1's only finding was on the fix's 'blob/master' URL, with a wrong premise but a better alternative. The agent checked the premise against the repo's real default branch before taking the alternative. Round 1 was still needed to review the new test file, so it is not counted as avoidable.
guidance_observations: The original PR added parsing logic without unit tests; new logic in a docs-flavored PR still needs its tests in round 0.
The agent's F3 reply is the right handling of a wrong premise bundled with a useful suggestion: verify the premise, then take the alternative on its merits.
